name: City Centre
description: The heart of Bishkek around Ala-Too Square, Chuy Avenue and the main museums. Wide Soviet-era boulevards, ministries, cafes and hotels sit here, with the State History Museum and Oak Park within walking distance. It is the most connected part of the city.
bestFor: First-time visitors wanting landmarks, cafes and transport nearby
cons: Traffic and noise on main avenues

name: Osh Bazaar Area
description: The western district around Osh Bazaar, one of the city's largest markets. It is crowded, lively and practical, full of food stalls, produce and cheap eateries. Marshrutkas radiate from here, making it a busy hub for daily life and budget shopping.
bestFor: Budget travellers wanting cheap food and authentic market life

name: Erkindik Boulevard
description: The tree-lined Erkindik Boulevard runs south from the centre, a pleasant pedestrian promenade with benches, the Fine Arts Museum and the old railway station at its end. Quieter and greener than the main avenues, it is popular for walks and slower cafe stops.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting quiet, walkable, cafe-lined streets

name: Yug-2 and Southern Districts
description: The southern residential microdistricts such as Yug-2, built in Soviet apartment blocks and closer to the Ala-Too foothills. It is quieter and cheaper than the centre, favoured by longer-stay renters, with local shops and easy access to mountain day trips.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting cheaper rent and mountain access
